design: 368 IRI panel households choosing among five grocery/mass retail chains in Charlotte, NC (Sept 2002-Sept 2004); no treatment, no adoption dates, no comparison group.
reason: The paper estimates a structural mixed nested logit of store choice and category incidence with a spatial ideal-point parameterization by simulated maximum likelihood (Section 6; Tables 5-6). Tables 7-9 are post-estimation decompositions and counterfactual merchandising scores. There is no policy change, binary treatment, or difference-in-differences anywhere in the article.
appendix_only_specs: none (web appendix holds identification proofs, merchandising parameter estimates, and CDI splits)
notes: Pure structural choice model; 'natural experiment' in Section 5.1 is only a descriptive recomputation of CDIs by spend group, not a causal design.
data_statement: No availability statement; data provided by Information Resources, Inc. (proprietary scanner panel), and interview information is available by contacting the third author.

notes: If the original Wlomert et al. (2023) Frontiers article is in the candidate pool, screen it separately; this rejoinder adds no specification.
data_statement: No data or code availability statement; Table 1 comes from thetrichordist.com (2020), and acknowledgments note an anonymous music label provided data access for the original study.
